answer: Copying the same citations across 139 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 139 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the prism index resolves every citation against the horizon checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the harbor audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 32 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
